page.layout: Two parallel columns of text on one page: the left column is the main text, the right column is a narrower column of short ragged lines beside it. No margin notes. Above the text: running head and page number at the top right. Below the text: signature at the bottom left, catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: lib.2.cap.19. e Æginetæ oximelite conditas lau-dat. e Attius ace o 6 oleo conditas ad excitan-dum appetitum coctionem q, iuuandam nobilif-simas (esse ait, minorig[?], negotio à ventriculo perfi-ci,quæ iucundiores sunt.

Acerbæ enim & virides omnes crudæ, nam certissimum[?] est omnem acerbitatem difficillimè domari ac vinci, ē Albas oliuas (quæ scilicet mediæ sunt inter virides & maturas, quarum illæ acerbæ sunt haueo[?], quæ & nigræ sunt, stomachum suâ pinguedine relaxant) sto-macho utiles esse prodiderunt Plin.lib.23.cap.3. Cels.lib.4.cap.20. Galen.s.de compos.me-dic. secundum loc. necnon Oribasius libr.7. Omnes enim bis in stomacho astringendo utun-tur.

Villis enim stomachi relaxatis appetitus per-ditur, & ventriculus sit debilis, corroboratur iidem astrictis. Quæ igitur magis astringunt, se-cundis mensis adhibendæ sunt, vt roborato ore ventriculi deorsum pellantur catera cibaria. Sed hodie eruditi pariter atque inerudiri, pri-mo,medio & postremo cibo,vt carnibus, piscibusq, eas sine vllo discrimine intermiscunt, (Capparis fructus crudi stomacho nocent,quare cuctos prius,deinde ex oleo & aceto mandere seos conuenit, sic enim appetitum excitant pituitam, in ventriculo incidunt, arq, educunt. Continuus Capparum vsus difficulter vrinam, neruæ sa-red dentibus podagricis,plenetico, magno ad-cra fit.

Olei ex oliuis fa-culrates omnes explicare nemo po-teft,adeo frequens multi-plexq; e-ius vius est. Ipfa autem o-lea apud veteres Romãos tante fuit autorita-tis, vt lex lata fuerit,quà cautum erat, ne quis oleã stringeret, pro-pterea q illa Mi-netuæ sacra fit.

page.notes: Right column: no clear paragraph breaks; set as one paragraph. Uncertain readings: running head (PROROGANDA), "certissimum", "haueo", "minorig", the first word of the left column line 17 ("Villis"), the catchword and signature at the foot. Left column line 25 "(Capparis" and line 29 "(continuus" begin with an opening bracket as printed; the text there is partly illegible, and the right-column lines near "Minetuæ" may be misread. Long s has been rendered as plain s throughout. Printing errors left as printed.
